What is the normal evolution (and phases) of appendicitis❓🍒
a:
obstruction → continous secretion of appendiceal mucosa → ↑intraluminal pressure → distension → pain

→ rapid multiplication of local appendix bacteria → edema, hyperemia, pentration through musosa = catarrhal appendicitis

→ spreads to serosa + peritoneum(locally) → Pain illiac fossa → Mc-burney's

→ phlegmonous phase → enlarged congested, purulent fluid on serosa + thickend mesoappendic

→ compression arterial blood flow → necrosis = gangrenous appendicitis

⇒ perforation

→ appendicular abcess,

→ appendicular block,

→ diffuse peritonitis (Rebound tenderness)

q: Acute appendicitis: How do you perform the operation❓🍒
a:
1. intraperitoneal examination
  2. free appendix from cecum
  3. ligation + transection mesoappendix
  4. ligation + transection of appendix base
  5. remove appendix + close wound

q: Appendicitis which blood values and what do you see in ultrasound ?

a:
• Primary symptom  abdominal pain

  • Associated symptoms  nausea, anorexia, transit disorders (constipation/diarrhea), fever (<38)

  • RLQ pain

  • Physical Exam  McBurney’s Point, voluntary guarding, muscular rigidity,

    • Possible tenderness on rectal palpation

    • Rovsing, Bloomberg, Psoas, Obturator signs

    • Dieulafoy’s sign  cuteanous hyperesthesia

  • Murphy’s Traid  pain right iliac fossa, vomiting, fever

  • Imaging  Xray, US, CT
